results.content: Motivated by applications in reinforcement learning (RL), we study a nonlinear stochastic approximation (SA) algorithm under Markovian noise, and establish its finite-sample convergence bounds under various stepsizes. To demonstrate the generality of our theoretical results on Markovian SA, we use it to derive the finite-sample bounds of the popular -learning algorithm with linear function approximation, under a condition on the behavior policy. Large-scale optimization and machine learning problems are often solved using stochastic approximation (SA) methods (i.e., iterative algorithms in the presence of noise). In RL, algorithms such as -learning, TD-learning, and actor–critic use sample trajectories generated from a Markov decision process (MDP) to carry out the update, and hence can also be modeled as Markovian SA algorithms. The asymptotic convergence of SA algorithms with Markovian noise has been studied extensively in the literature (Benveniste et al., 2012, Bertsekas and Tsitsiklis, 1996, Borkar, 2009). **Finite-Sample Analysis for Nonlinear Markovian SA.** We establish finite-sample convergence guarantees for nonlinear SA with Markovian noise for using various stepsizes, where we do not require an artificial projection step in the algorithm. **Finite-Sample Analysis of *Q*-Learning with Linear Function Approximation.** To demonstrate the effectiveness of our SA results, we use them to establish for the first time finite-sample bounds for -learning under linear function approximation. For linear SA algorithms, finite-sample mean-square bounds were established under either i.i.d. sampling or Markovian sampling in Bhandari, Russo, and Singal (2018) and Srikant and Ying (2019). ***Q*-Learning (with Linear Function Approximation).** -learning (Watkins & Dayan, 1992) is perhaps one of the most popular algorithms for solving RL problems (Bertsekas and Tsitsiklis, 1996, Sutton and Barto, 2018). In this work, we consider -learning under linear function approximation, which can be modeled as a nonlinear Markovian SA algorithm (Melo, Meyn, & Ribeiro, 2008). In this paper we establish finite-sample convergence guarantees for a general nonlinear SA algorithm with Markovian noise. The result is used to derive, for the first time, finite-sample bounds for -learning with linear function approximation. ### Residual algorithms: Reinforcement learning with function approximation. results.content: Finite-sample analysis of nonlinear stochastic approximation with applications in reinforcement learning. ## Details. Finite-sample analysis of nonlinear stochastic approximation with applications in reinforcement learning. ## Comprehensive Info. ## Abstract. Motivated by applications in reinforcement learning (RL), we study a nonlinear stochastic approximation (SA) algorithm under Markovian noise, and establish its finite-sample convergence bounds under various stepsizes. Specifically, we show that when using constant stepsize (i.e., αk≡α), the algorithm achieves exponential fast convergence to a neighborhood (with radius O(αlog(1/α))) around the desired limit point. When using diminishing stepsizes with appropriate decay rate, the algorithm converges with rate O(log(k)/k). Our proof is based on Lyapunov drift arguments, and to handle the Markovian noise, we exploit the fast mixing of the underlying Markov chain. To demonstrate the generality of our theoretical results on Markovian SA, we use it to derive the finite-sample bounds of the popular Q-learning algorithm with linear function approximation, under a condition on the behavior policy. Importantly, we do not need to make the assumption that the samples are i.i.d., and do not require an artificial projection step in the algorithm. Numerical simulations corroborate our theoretical results. ## References. ## Cited by. ## Related articles Refresh. ## Journal Information. 京公网安备11010802045318号京ICP备20010051号-16京ICP备20010051号-15津ICP备2023003620号-1营业执照增值电信业务经营许可证合字B2-20210408网信算备110108025106801240015号.
